name: Whole-country dark
statement: We need the site connected to the internet, full stop.

name: Signal there, can't afford it
statement: We need connectivity we can actually afford to keep switched on.

name: Facilities unmapped
statement: We need a trusted, complete map of every facility before we can plan anything.

name: Data never comes together
statement: We need one place where all our connectivity data comes together.

name: Flying blind on cost
statement: We need a real cost and technology estimate before we commit budget.

name: Data never reaches decision
statement: We need our data to reach decision-makers while it still matters.

name: No one watching the line
statement: We need to know in real time if a connection goes down.

name: 'Good enough' data complacency
statement: We need a reason and a moment to upgrade past data we only think is good enough.

name: Unverified data trusted as fact
statement: We need our connectivity data independently verified, not just self-reported.

name: Facility registry drift
statement: We need our facility registry refreshed regularly, not just built once and left to go stale.

name: No proof, no money
statement: We need credible proof of impact before we can unlock funding.

name: Bill bigger than any budget
statement: We need a financing plan that spreads the cost across more than one source.

name: Cable isn't the whole bill
statement: We need the full cost — not just the cable — reflected in the budget from the start.

name: Nobody pays after ribbon-cutting
statement: We need a funded plan for who pays to keep this running, not just to switch it on.

name: Locked out of the AI era
statement: We need infrastructure that's ready for what comes after basic connectivity, not just today's needs.

name: Power keeps cutting out
statement: We need stable power before connectivity can mean anything.

name: Everything missing at once
statement: We need a plan that tackles power, backbone and devices together, not one at a time.

name: Backbone isn't built
statement: We need the backbone infrastructure built before last-mile connections are even possible.

name: No grid to plug into
statement: We need an off-grid power solution, because the grid isn't coming.

name: No digital skills, no job
statement: We need digital skills training alongside the connection, not instead of it.

name: Cable alone changes nothing
statement: We need devices, training and content — not just a cable — for connectivity to matter.

name: Nothing to plug skills into
statement: We need the connectivity that makes the skills we already have usable.

name: Digitisation excludes least skilled
statement: We need digitisation designed so it doesn't leave the least digitally confident behind.

name: One doctor for 12,000
statement: We need more trained frontline staff, and connectivity-enabled ways to stretch the ones we have.

name: Internet without guidance backfires
statement: We need guidance and safeguards to go live at the same time as the connection.

name: Staff can't run the programme
statement: We need hands-on capacity support to run this, not just the funding to start it.

name: Development blocked without connectivity
statement: We need connectivity so our own staff can access the training they need.

name: More access, more exposure
statement: We need safety measures that scale up alongside access, not after it.

name: No shared safety rulebook
statement: We need one shared, enforceable child-safety standard everyone can be held to.

name: No affordable filter at scale
statement: We need content filtering that small providers can actually afford.

name: Safeguards bolted on after
statement: We need safety built into the plan from day one, not patched on afterward.

name: Citizens fear for their data
statement: We need people to be able to trust what happens to their data.

name: Protection can't reach offline children
statement: We need protection systems that can reach children even before they're connected.

name: Weak procurement drives up cost
statement: We need stronger procurement capacity so we're not overpaying by default.

name: Last-mile uneconomical
statement: We need an incentive or subsidy that makes the last mile worth an operator's while.

name: No enforcement on suppliers
statement: We need contracts with teeth — a real way to hold suppliers accountable.

name: Regulators lack standards to enforce
statement: We need enforceable standards regulators can actually hold providers to.

name: Rules built for big, static operators
statement: We need spectrum rules that make room for new kinds of providers, not just incumbents.

name: Operators lack certainty to invest
statement: We need predictable rules so operators feel safe investing for the long term.

name: Crisis cuts the line
statement: We need connectivity that holds up during emergencies, not just in normal conditions.

name: Connected on paper only
statement: We need connections that are actually usable, not just technically present.

name: Service degrades without it
statement: We need service delivery that doesn't collapse the moment connectivity dips.

name: Health system runs on paper
statement: We need digital record-keeping that actually replaces the paper trail.

name: No plan to restore it
statement: We need a clear plan for restoring connectivity fast when it fails.

name: A dropped connection can kill
statement: We need connectivity reliable enough that losing it isn't a matter of life and death.

name: Preventable deaths
statement: We need connected care that stops these deaths from being preventable and still happening.

name: Income & opportunity lost
statement: We need connectivity that turns into real income and opportunity, not just access.

name: Learning & life chances lost
statement: We need connectivity that closes the learning gap, not just adds a wire to the classroom.

name: Cost of inaction, quantified
statement: We need the quantified cost of inaction put in front of the people who decide budgets.

name: Proof demanded by funders
statement: We need a credible, funder-ready evidence package before we ask for money.

name: No causal proof
statement: We need real causal evidence that connectivity is what's driving the outcome, not just a correlation.

name: Each ministry buys alone
statement: We need ministries planning connectivity together, not each buying it alone.

name: Pile of tools, no standards
statement: We need our health data tools to actually talk to each other.

name: Nobody owns the pathway
statement: We need one clear owner responsible for the whole pathway, start to finish.

name: No standards to align around
statement: We need a shared standard everyone can build to, instead of everyone inventing their own.

name: Evidence with no enforcement teeth
statement: We need evidence that's tied to a real decision, payment, or enforcement action, not just a report that sits on a shelf.

name: Incentives work against adoption
statement: We need governance and incentives that reward better data practice instead of treating it as extra burden.

name: No scandal on my watch
statement: We need airtight safety measures so this never becomes a scandal on anyone's watch.

name: Country not left behind
statement: We need visible proof our country is keeping pace, not falling behind.

name: Felt benefits, not promises
statement: We need people to feel the difference this makes, not just hear that it happened.

name: Same children left behind, again
statement: We need this rollout to deliberately reach the children every previous effort left out.

name: AI hype crowds out access
statement: We need basic access funded and protected even while AI captures the spotlight.

name: Nationally led, not imposed
statement: We need this to be visibly our agenda, led by us, not imposed from outside.

name: The message gets misheard
statement: We need our message to land as intended with audiences who think in economic terms, not get lost in translation.

name: Show lived experience, not intent
statement: We need to show real lived experience, not just describe our intentions.

name: Treated as beneficiaries, not actors
statement: We need young people treated as active participants, not passive recipients.

name: Tokenistic participation
statement: We need participation that's genuinely built into decisions, not just a box we tick.

name: The system doesn't listen
statement: We need institutions people can trust are actually listening to them.
